summary: Beyond the Sun is a card-driven space tech-tree game where players spend action pawns to research technologies, build economy, and colonize systems, racing to trigger and claim shared end-game achievements. It plays quickly for its depth, with the branching tech tree giving each game a distinct shape depending on which paths players prioritize.
praised: Elegant, branching tech tree that creates real strategic choices
No player elimination and relatively low downtime for a civ-style game
Smooth, well-paced turns despite meaningful depth
criticised: Can feel like multiplayer solitaire with limited direct interaction
Dense iconography and rules text on the tech cards early on
Colonization/area-influence layer feels somewhat secondary to the tech engine

interaction.kind: area majority and shared tech tree race
interaction.detail: Players move influence onto a shared galactic map of star systems, contesting the same systems for area-majority control, and research technologies from a shared tech tree where researching a tech can trigger effects for everyone and remove options for others. There is no direct attack or piece capture; interaction is through claiming shared map territory and shared technology slots before opponents do.

sources: VP printed on researched technology cards
scoring.how_you_win: Each turn you research a technology, which both advances your economy/colonization and can score points directly; the game ends once enough achievements are collectively claimed, and the player with the most accumulated VP from tech, colonies and achievements wins.

similar: Eclipse: Second Dawn for the Galaxy
